Safety inspection checklist
Use the information in this section to identify potentially unsafe conditions with your rack solution. As each 
machine was designed and built, required safety items were installed to protect users and service 
technicians from injury.
Note: The product is not suitable for use at visual display workplaces according to §2 of the Workplace 
Regulations.
Note: The set-up of the rack solution is made in the server room only.
CAUTION: 
This equipment must be serviced by trained personnel, as defined by the IEC 62368-1, the standard for 
Safety of Electronic Equipment within the Field of Audio/Video, Information Technology and 
Communication Technology. Lenovo assumes you are qualified in the servicing of equipment and 
trained in recognizing hazards energy levels in products. Equipment must be installed in a restricted 
access location and access to the equipment is controlled by the authority responsible for the 
location.
Important: Electrical grounding of the rack solution is required for operator safety and correct system 
function. Proper grounding of the electrical outlet can be verified by a certified electrician.
Use the following checklist to verify that there are no potentially unsafe conditions: 
1. Make sure that the power is off and the power cord is disconnected.
2. Check the power cord.
• Make sure that the third-wire ground connector is in good condition. Use a meter to measure third- 
wire ground continuity for 0.1 ohm or less between the external ground pin and the frame ground.
• Make sure that the power cord is the correct type. 
To view the power cords that are available for the rack solution:

Chapter 1. Introduction
The Lenovo NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 (Type 7DJV) is a revolutionary, liquid-cooled rack-scale solution that 
integrates seventy-two high-performance Blackwell Ultra GPUs and thirty-six Grace processors into a single, 
unified system. This liquid-cooled powerhouse represents the pinnacle of Generative AI infrastructure, 
featuring the NVLink Switch System which enables all seventy-two GPUs to communicate as a single, 
massive autonomous engine. With high-speed PCIe 6.0 connectivity and fifth-generation NVLink technology, 
the solution provides unprecedented bandwidth and ultra-low latency data transfer across the entire fabric. 
Designed to solve the world’s most complex challenges, it is engineered to accelerate trillion-parameter AI 
model training, real-time inference, and massive-scale scientific simulations.
Figure 1. Lenovo NVIDIA GB300 NVL72
Features
Performance, operational efficiency, and fabric reliability were the primary considerations in the design of the 
rack solution.
The rack solution implements the following features and technologies: 
• High HBM3e bandwidth

The rack solution utilizes HBM3e technology to deliver a total of 20.7 TB of HBM3e across the 72-GPU 
NVLink domain. This allows the system to process large AI models instantly and handle massive scientific 
data.
• High network bandwidth
The rack solution features high-speed networking via NVIDIA BlueField-3 DPU adapters or ConnectX-8 
SuperNICs. This integrated architecture provides massive aggregate bandwidth across the entire rack, 
ensuring seamless data flow for large-scale AI workloads.
• Large system-memory capacity
The system utilizes a unified memory architecture featuring LPDDR5X memory with error correcting code 
(ECC) integrated directly onto the NVIDIA Grace processor. This provides up to 17.3 TB of system 
memory per rack.
• Large data-storage capacity and hot-swap capability
Each compute tray supports high-speed E1.S drives, providing localized data staging. With the hot-swap 
feature, you can add, remove, or replace solid-state drives without turning off the compute tray.
• Lightpath Diagnostics
Lightpath Diagnostics provides LEDs to help you diagnose problems. For more information about the 
Lightpath Diagnostics, see “Troubleshooting by system LEDs and diagnostics display” on page 23.
Tech Tips
Lenovo continually updates the support website with the latest tips and techniques that you can use to solve 
issues that your rack solution might encounter. These Tech Tips (also called retain tips or service bulletins) 
provide procedures to work around issues or solve problems related to the operation of your rack solution.
To find the Tech Tips available for your rack solution: 
1. Go to http://datacentersupport.lenovo.com and navigate to the support page for your rack solution.
2. Click on How To’s from the navigation pane.
3. Click Article Type ➙ Solution from the drop-down menu.
Follow the on-screen instructions to choose the category for the problem that you are having.

Risks that are posed by the presence of excessive particulate levels or concentrations of harmful gases 
include damage that might cause the device to malfunction or cease functioning altogether. This 
specification sets forth limits for particulates and gases that are intended to avoid such damage. The limits

contaminant transfer. In the absence of specific limits that are set forth in this document, you must 
implement practices that maintain particulate and gas levels that are consistent with the protection of human 
health and safety. If Lenovo determines that the levels of particulates or gases in your environment have 
caused damage to the device, Lenovo may condition provision of repair or replacement of devices or parts

Update Bundles (Service Packs)
Lenovo typically releases firmware in bundles called Update Bundles (Service Packs). To ensure that all of

Update method terminology
• In-band update. The installation or update is performed using a tool or application within an operating 
system that is executing on the server’s core CPU.
• Out-of-band update. The installation or update is performed by the HOST BMC, collecting the update 
and then directing the update to the target subsystem or device. Out-of-band updates have no 
dependency on an operating system executing on the core CPU. However, most out-of-band operations 
do require the server to be in the S0 (Working) power state.
• On-Target update. The installation or update is initiated from an installed operating system executing on 
the target server itself.
• Update Bundles (Service Packs). Update Bundles (Service Packs) are bundled updates designed and 
tested to provide the interdependent level of functionality, performance, and compatibility. Update 
Bundles (Service Packs) are server machine-type specific and are built (with firmware and device driver 
updates) to support specific Windows Server, Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) and SUSE Linux 
Enterprise Server (SLES) operating system distributions. Machine-type-specific firmware-only Update 
Bundles (Service Packs) are also available.
